notes: The 10-year US interest rate (5.24%) is 1.15% above the 3-month rate (4.09%), and that gap has widened by 0.47% in 3 months: often a sign that growth is picking up.
Copper and gold have moved about the same over 3 months (+3.0% for copper vs gold): no strong growth signal.
Fear gauge (VIX) at 15.9: markets are calm (under 16 = calm, over 25 = stressed).
The US stock market (S&P 500) is above its average price over the last 200 trading days (about 10 months): its long-term uptrend is intact.

todaysConditions.note: Oil is up 31% over 3 months: a boost for markets full of oil and gas companies, and a cost for countries that import a lot of oil.

The fear gauge (VIX) is a calm 15.9 (18 or less), and world stocks are 6.0% above their average price over the last 200 trading days (about 10 months). When investors feel confident, emerging markets usually benefit.
Chip-maker shares did 8.4% worse than world stocks over 3 months: a drag on tech-heavy markets.
